title: A/B Test Judge
instruction: Can you trust this result? (Conversion = the share of users who bought, clicked or engaged.)

items.text: A: 10,000 users, 12% bought. B: 10,000 users, 8% bought.
items.why: A 4-point gap on 10,000 users per group is far beyond what chance produces (p far below 0.001).

items.text: A: 100,000 users, 3.1% converted. B: 100,000 users, 3.5% converted.
items.why: A small lift on a huge sample is real: chance alone would produce it far less than once in a thousand tests (p well below 0.001). Whether it is worth shipping is a separate question.

items.text: A: 5,000 users, 25% engaged. B: 5,000 users, 15% engaged.
items.why: A large gap on a decent sample: chance does not produce this.

items.text: A: 20 users, 5 liked it. B: 20 users, 8 liked it.
items.why: With 20 users per group, a gap this size appears by chance about 3 times in 10 (p ≈ 0.31).

items.text: A: 1,000 users, 52% clicked. B: 1,000 users, 48% clicked.
items.why: Close, but not past the usual 5% bar (p ≈ 0.07). Collect more data or accept the uncertainty.

items.text: Week 1: B is +8% on clicks. Week 4: +0.5% and still falling.
items.why: A novelty effect: the early lift fades. There is no evidence of a lasting gain yet.

items.text: B looked significant on day 2, so the team stopped early and shipped it.
items.why: Peeking: stopping the moment the result looks good inflates false positives far above 5%.

items.text: The team checked 12 metrics; one of them improved with p = 0.04.
items.why: Multiple testing: with 12 independent tries, the chance of at least one lucky 'win' is about 46%. Pre-register one primary metric.

items.text: A ran on weekdays, B on the weekend.
items.why: Not concurrent: the day of the week, not the variant, may explain the gap.

items.text: Users chose for themselves whether to try the new recommender.
items.why: No random assignment: people who volunteer differ from everyone else.

debrief: An A/B test is only as good as its design: random assignment, both variants at the same time, a sample size fixed in advance, one primary metric, and enough time to outlast novelty.
